questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere that was in a big city, that was different from what I know and an english speaking country. Furthermore, I mostly chose Toronto because of the academic opportunities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall I had a good and fun experience, but I lived a bit far from campus and I had an insane amount of work for university, which ended up taking up a lot of time, even though I learned a lot

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to know what to do in a practical sense, and it was a smooth start to all my courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an introductory meeting at the university with other international students, showings around campus and a lot of emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Even though it was easy to navigate, it would ahve been nice to see more organized events for us to meet people when we arrive.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy, living on campus or close to campus while on exchange is very difficult. It is also difficult to get a lease for under a year unless its through Airbnb. I found the place on Airbnb but ended up signing a lease outside of the company to avoid service costs.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is difficult to find something prior to 2-3 months before arriving, because things are not available at that time. Living on campus is super expensive and almost impossible. Harrington housing and Tartu college are popular places where exchange students live but hard to get into. Uofts off-housing website has some good offers and also puts up announcements for subleases. Otherwise your best bet is facebook or airbnb to start with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very stressful to find a place, but in the end everyone finds something, so dont worry! it is also very common to move around during your exchange.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it very easy, there is a lot to keep track of and especially choosing courses and getting them approved was a very time-consuming process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get approved by KU, then you have to send a formal application to the university, get courses approved and follow the steps on mobility online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a coordinator for Canada who was available to answer questions, and a facebook group was set up for students going to Canada to communicate with each other.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got preapproved for 15 courses, and only four of them ended up being available for the semester, so there was not much of a choice to be made  in my case.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When you apply for courses, KU approves as many as 15 courses, and since when you are doing this the academic timetable for the term when youre going on exchange (fall 2023 in my case) is not availbale yet, so you have to choose based on the calendar of the current year. I recommend applying for as many courses as you can, since anything can happen and that way you have more to choose from.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I enjoyed most of my courses a lot, the amount of work was a bit much from my courses, as in KU we are used to not having much more than the final exam and some occasional reports, here I had multiple deadlines, essays and quizzes almost every week. I did learn a lot though and found the program very interesting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one level 4 course, one level 2 course and one level 3 course. I found that the level for my level 3 courses was adequate, the level 4 course was very complicated and had a lot more workload, while the level 2 course was much easier. These two balanced each other out, but I definitely 100% recommend considering level 4 courses thoroughly before choosing them, if you are a year 3 student, because the difference in level was quite clear, and most canadian students do not tak emore than 2 level 4 courses at the same time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As i mentioned, I feel that we were not treated with as much independence and had more homework .

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Confronting global change, Ecosystem ecology, Principles of ecological agroforestry, Topics in applied conservation.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Ecosystem ecology was a great course, it included a field trip and a lot of fun lab excercises. The teacher, Shelby Riskin, remembers all her students names and creates a very intimate atmosphere in the classroom. The workload was not too bad, it was mostly done in groups, and we had no final exam which was nice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The transport is really expensive, and having a social life as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is less expensive than copenhagen, but groceries are more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved hart houses creative thursdays, where I learned to tye dye, make buttons, and I often went to drop in yoga classes.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a toon of activities on campus, both non-competitive sports teams (intramurals), drop-in fitness classes of all sorts in the 3 gyms on campus, and countless clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend the uTOC club, an outdoor club that organizes activities in nature off campus. I went kayaking with them and on a weekend cabin trip by the blue mountains, which was a great experience. If you enjoy running then the running club is also a nice way to see the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go for brunch, visit the parks and islands before it gets too cold, and honestly just walk around and explore neighborhoods.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not that hard, I had to get used to people not having their main friends in their classes and the campus life.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Its easy to talk to people if youre not shy, but making friends with locals is always mroe difficult than with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The student life is very different from back home, it is way more challenging and people spend a lot more time studying.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated how international it was, you meet people and cultures from all over the world, which is safe to say we are missing in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Try to find housing in the city, I regretted living so far from campus. 
- Use the campus and all the non-academic opportunities
- Have fun and dont worry too much about doing too much all the time, it is going to be very intense and fun so taking days for yourself is a good investment.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose things you think might be fun because you might end up spending a lot of time on them:)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: What I learned on my courses and the people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing studying with work life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
